title: Measurement uncertainty and propagation through an inference
reasoning_question: What uncertainty does a conclusion inherit from measured inputs?
inputs: A defined measurand Y=f(X), input estimates, covariance and calibration information.
conclusions: An estimate with combined standard uncertainty under a specified measurement model; coverage claims only with justified distribution/coverage assumptions.
assumptions: Measurand and units fixed; corrections distinguished from uncertainty; dependence preserved; linearization justified over the uncertainty range.

required_components.description: Specify the measurand and measurement equation; distinguish error, correction and uncertainty.
required_components.success_condition: Give an explicit quantity, units, input roles and uncertain corrections.
required_components.failure_condition: Treat uncertainty as an observed error or the standard deviation as every source of uncertainty.

required_components.failure_condition: Use the independent-input formula for shared calibration errors or declare the Taylor approximation exact.

required_components.failure_condition: Call Type B subjective error without an assigned information model or equate the two classifications.

title: Dimensional and scaling constraints on quantitative claims
reasoning_question: Which quantitative relationships are possible given dimensions and scaling assumptions?
inputs: Declared physical quantities, units/dimensions and a proposed governing-variable set.
conclusions: Admissible dimensionless forms and scaling relations conditional on the complete variable set and invariance assumptions; no numerical constant or empirical law from dimensions alone.
assumptions: Dimensions are consistently assigned; the selected variables include relevant dimensional quantities; dimension-matrix rank is used.

required_components.description: Construct dimensionless products as a linear nullspace problem.
required_components.success_condition: Solve a dimension matrix and explain the rank-dependent count of independent products.
required_components.failure_condition: Subtract the number of written dimension names without checking rank.

required_components.description: Use proportional reasoning to separate exponents from constants.
required_components.success_condition: Derive an admissible exponent relation and identify what remains empirically undetermined.
required_components.failure_condition: Present dimensional consistency as proof of the physical law.

title: Approximate conclusions, limiting regimes and explicit error
reasoning_question: When does an approximation justify the conclusion being drawn?
inputs: An exact or stipulated model, a target output, a small/large dimensionless parameter and tolerated error.
conclusions: A regime-specific approximation or bound whose status and error permit the particular comparison or prediction.
assumptions: The limit, fixed variables and approximation type are declared; numerical, model and statistical errors are distinguished.

required_components.description: Distinguish identity, bound, asymptotic equivalence and heuristic estimate.
required_components.success_condition: State the relation used and its domain before drawing the output conclusion.
required_components.failure_condition: Use an asymptotic sign as an exact equality or an informal estimate as a proven interval.

required_components.description: Develop lumping and limiting-case reasoning in bounded examples.
required_components.success_condition: Reconstruct selected characteristic-value and two-regime cases with their assumptions.
required_components.failure_condition: Replace heterogeneous inputs by an average without testing the relevant nonlinearity.

required_components.failure_condition: Use a close approximate value to decide a sign smaller than the error.

title: Numerical error and the validity of computed conclusions
reasoning_question: Can a computed value support the claimed sign, ordering or accuracy?
inputs: A numerical expression or algorithm, input uncertainty, arithmetic format and rounding assumptions.
conclusions: A justified error budget for the computed conclusion, or a refusal to certify a sign/order when available error bounds overlap it.
assumptions: Arithmetic model and exceptional cases fixed; exact-input numerical error separated from uncertain-data sensitivity.

reasoning_question: Which aspects of observed data are incompatible with a proposed Bayesian model?
